acceptance_criteria.criterion: `Directory.Build.props` defines exactly one `<TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>` inside a `<PropertyGroup>` that applies solution-wide.
A repository-wide search for `<TargetFramework>` inside any `.csproj` returns zero matches.
A repository-wide search for `net8.0` inside any `.csproj` or build-config file returns zero matches.
A repository-wide search for `<RollForward>` returns zero matches.
`dotnet restore` against the solution completes successfully on the .NET 10 SDK.

summary: Pinned .NET 10.0.202 SDK with rollForward: latestFeature in global.json.
Added TargetFramework=net10.0 centrally in Directory.Build.props.
Removed <TargetFramework> from all 6 .csproj files (Core, Infrastructure, App, Tests, App.Tests, Infrastructure.Tests).
Removed <RollForward>LatestMajor</RollForward> from VideoIndexer.Tests.csproj and VideoIndexer.App.Tests.csproj.
Added NuGetAuditMode=direct to Directory.Build.props to suppress transitive vulnerability noise from Avalonia's Tmds.DBus.Protocol 0.20.0 (deferred to WP-002).
dotnet restore against VideoIndexer.sln completes cleanly on .NET 10 SDK.

comments.note: Tmds.DBus.Protocol 0.20.0 (transitive via Avalonia 11.2.5) has a known high severity vulnerability (GHSA-xrw6-gwf8-vvr9). NuGetAuditMode=direct was added as a temporary shield; the proper fix is upgrading Avalonia in WP-002.

VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests.csproj was already targeting net10.0 before this WP, suggesting it may have been partially migrated out-of-band. No impact on correctness, but worth noting for audit trail.

VideoIndexer.Tests.csproj and VideoIndexer.App.Tests.csproj carry <IsPackable>false</IsPackable> and <IsTestProject>true</IsTestProject>, but VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests.csproj only has <IsPackable>false</IsPackable> (no <IsTestProject>). Consider adding <IsTestProject>true</IsTestProject> for consistency — this is out of scope for WP-001.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified and confirmed met.
dotnet restore clean; solution build succeeds with 0 warnings and 0 errors (TreatWarningsAsErrors=true).
All build outputs land in net10.0/ directories for all 5 projects.
151 tests pass across 3 test assemblies (VideoIndexer.Tests: 47, VideoIndexer.App.Tests: 41, VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests: 63); 2 expected live/integration skips.
No <TargetFramework>, net8.0, or <RollForward> found in any .csproj or build-config file within the video-indexer-v2 workspace.

comments.note: The build-file lock on VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests CoreCompileInputs.cache occurred when running `dotnet test` with a fresh build immediately after `dotnet build` on the solution. Using `--no-build` on the Infrastructure test project resolved it. No impact on correctness; likely a transient MSBuild artifact contention issue on Windows.

VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests.csproj is missing <IsTestProject>true</IsTestProject> (noted by Developer). Not a blocker for this WP, but worth addressing for tooling consistency in a future cleanup pass.

NuGetAuditMode=direct suppresses the Tmds.DBus.Protocol 0.20.0 high-severity vulnerability (GHSA-xrw6-gwf8-vvr9). This is an intentional deferral to WP-002 (Avalonia upgrade). Confirm WP-002 removes this suppression once Avalonia is upgraded.

summary: WP-001 passes code review across all four dimensions: maintainability, best practices, performance, and future context.
global.json is correctly structured — SDK 10.0.202 pinned with rollForward:latestFeature. Semantically correct: will accept any 10.0.x patch/feature release, stops at 10.1.
Directory.Build.props is clean — single PropertyGroup, TargetFramework centralized, comment on NuGetAuditMode is clear and actionable (points to WP-002).

All 6 .csproj files are correctly stripped of TargetFramework. Source projects carry only project-specific properties; test projects correctly override TreatWarningsAsErrors with explanatory comments.

Fix-Forward applied: added <IsTestProject>true</IsTestProject> to VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests.csproj for tooling consistency with the other two test projects. Non-behavioral — QA validation remains intact.
No blocking issues found. NuGetAuditMode=direct debt shield is correctly scoped and documented. The vulnerability (GHSA-xrw6-gwf8-vvr9) is deferred to WP-002 per design.

comments.note: Added <IsTestProject>true</IsTestProject> to tests/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests.csproj. The other two test projects (VideoIndexer.Tests, VideoIndexer.App.Tests) both carry this property; its absence was a tooling consistency gap flagged independently by both Developer and QA. This property has no effect on compilation or test execution — it is purely a metadata hint consumed by IDEs and test runners.

NuGetAuditMode=direct is a deliberate debt shield for Avalonia's transitive Tmds.DBus.Protocol 0.20.0 (GHSA-xrw6-gwf8-vvr9). Confirm WP-002 removes this line once Avalonia is upgraded to a version that resolves the transitive dependency.

VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.csproj references Microsoft.Extensions.* packages at 8.0.x versions and Serilog.Extensions.Hosting at 8.0.0. These are not aligned with net10.0. Package upgrade alignment is out of scope for WP-001 but should be addressed in WP-002 or WP-003.

[documentation-forward] Directory.Build.props contains the NuGetAuditMode=direct suppression comment referencing WP-002. README or CHANGELOG should note this intentional suppression and its resolution path so future contributors are not confused by the non-default audit mode.
